subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Njeri Kamau (1924-1998) was a jazz saxophonist born in Nairobi, Kenya.
• She had Kikuyu and Swahili heritage and trained in both traditional East African music and Western jazz.
• She was the first Kenyan-born musician to perform at the Newport Jazz Festival.
• Early in her career, she wrote many unrecorded pieces performed only in Nairobi clubs, such as 'Savanna Blues' (1948).
• Later, she composed many studio-released works, such as the title track of her album 'Mombasa Nights' (1971).
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the two compositions were written. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Njeri Kamau was celebrated for compositions like 'Savanna Blues' (1948) and 'Mombasa Nights' (1971).
choices.B: 'Savanna Blues' (1948) was written early in Njeri Kamau's career, whereas 'Mombasa Nights' (1971) was composed years later.
choices.C: 'Savanna Blues' (1948) was an unrecorded piece Njeri Kamau performed only in Nairobi clubs; however, 'Mombasa Nights' (1971) was a studio-released work that appeared on one of her albums.
choices.D: Early in her career, Njeri Kamau wrote pieces that were never recorded, such as 'Savanna Blues,' which she performed only in Nairobi clubs.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the order in which the two compositions were written, noting that 'Savanna Blues' was written early in Kamau's career (1948) and that 'Mombasa Nights' was composed years later (1971).

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The sentence only mentions 'Savanna Blues'; it doesn't mention 'Mombasa Nights' or emphasize the order in which the two compositions were written.
